characters.name: Robin
characters.description: The self-appointed leader of the Teen Titans. His overbearing attitude often annoys his teammates. He has an unrequited crush on Starfire. Abhorrent Admirer: Unlike the original series, where the attraction was clearly mutual, it's repeatedly shown that Starfire not only has no interest in him, but is genuinely repulsed by his presence, though she may have some feelings for him after all,depending on what episode you watch. The Ace: Robin tries to sell himself off as one, constantly emphasizing on his many talents. His claim seems to be at least partly true, as he's a skilled martial artist, inventor, infiltrator and business man. This served as the central focus in "Multiple Trick Pony". Adaptational Angst Upgrade: This Robin appears to have had a moreDark and Troubled Past—he has bad memories of his childhood from his circus days and forwhatever reasonhe's terrified of Batman. All of this may have contributed to this Robin being more unhinged. Adaptational Curves: Inverted. This Robin is practically devoid of any muscle mass, aside from those rare instances ofFan Disservicewhere he's suddenly ripped.

characters.name: Starfire
characters.description: Abusive Parents: In "Caramel Apples", Starfire mentions that her father was neglectful. Adaptational Badass: On top of retaining all her powers from the 2003 cartoon, this Starfire also possessesSuper-Speedto levels her 2003 cartoon counterpart never had. It's sometimes implied she can reach FTL speeds. Adaptational Dumbass: In the 2003 cartoon, Starfire wasn't exactly "dumb", as she was just an alien who was new to earth and was shown to be rather smart. This Starfire had her intelligence taken down to the extent that she is just as idiotic as Robin, Cyborg and Beast Boy. Adaptation Dye-Job: Her hair goes from red in the 2003 cartoon (and the comics) to a bright pink. And to add to that, it's now even longer than before. Adrenaline Makeover: Gets a beefier physique, tattoos (some of which she burned into her own skin using her powers), and a rough haircut during "Mr. Butt".

characters.name: Cyborg
characters.description: Half man, half machine, Cyborg serves as the muscle of the team. He's best friends with Beast Boy, and has a relationship with H.I.V.E. member Jinx. Abnormal Limb Rotation Range: Can swivel his head like an owl. Justified because he's mostly mechanical. Adaptational Badass: Now has farmore gadgetsand abilities than he did in the 2003 cartoon. Most notably, now he can fly via a jetpack. Adaptational Dumbass: He's much dumber than he is in the 2003 cartoon, where he was level headed, to complement Beast Boy already beingBook Dumband to set them up asThose Two Guys, though he occasionally has traits of his original self'sGadgeteer Geniuspersonality. Adaptational Jerkass: Like the other Titans, this version of Cyborg is much less mature and heroic and here he's just a selfish and immatureJerkass. He's also not above doing cruel things to achieve a selfish goal.

characters.name: Beast Boy
characters.description: Accidental Pervert: In "Mouth Hole", when Raven walks past him, someone whistles flirtatiously. Raven mistakes it for Beast Boy and slaps him, leading him to protest his innocence. Adaptational Badass: This Beast Boy appears to have a much greater control over his powers, being able rapidly change forms with no effort and spending far more time as an animal than his original self did. Oh, and he's now able totalk as an animallike in the comics. Adaptational Dumbass: Compared to his original version, this incarnation of Beast Boy has almost no common sense. Adaptational Intelligence: Played with. While his common sense and general knowledge are much lower than his 2003 cartoon counterpart, he displays more skill in talents of fine arts. He has a passion for poetry, can play the guitar, an excellent singer, and composed several songs with one of them gaining him renowed fame in "BBRae". Adaptational Jerkass: While Beast Boy was always depicted as a rebel, this Beast Boy is noticeably more of a jerk than his former incarnation, and is often devoid of remorse and regret over his actions. Instead of feeling guilty for his pranks, he will often laugh and fail to comprehend he has done anything wrong.

characters.name: Raven
characters.description: Actor Allusion: Her obsession withPretty Pretty Pegasusis a reference to Tara becoming well-known for voicingTwilight Sparklein the intervening years between the 2003 cartoon and this series. During the episode where Tara Strongplays herselfshe even does Twilight Sparkle's voice to Raven's awe. Actually Pretty Funny: While the other Titans are riffing on Robin for telling lame uncle jokes, Raven is the only one seen laughing and finding them genuinely funny. Adaptational Angst Downgrade: Her backstory wasn't actually as bad as her previous incarnation, in fact she used to live a happy life with her father. There instead seems to be angst coming from her teammates being annoying idiotic jerks and her having to constantly put up with them. Adaptational Badass: In the 2003 cartoon, Raven was a powerful spellcaster, but her magic haddefined limitsto them. In this show, her magic seems to have no restrictions and she's essentially a borderlineReality Warperwho can do virtually whatever she wants (or whatever the plot needs her to do). Adaptational Jerkass: This Raven has more anger management issues. She is prone to violent outbursts and has a habit of attacking the other Titans if annoyed, especially Beast Boy.

characters.name: Silkie
characters.description: Accidental Hero: In "La Larva de Amor" possibly. It's left ambiguous whether he meant to defeat Carlos or not. Adaptational Attractiveness: Silkie's cuteness got amped up 10-fold in this series. Adaptational Early Appearance: Silkie was introduced in the original series as early as the second season as a pet the Beast Boy sneaks into the tower and is eventually made into the Titans pet.Teen Titans Go!has him already being a pet of the Titans right from the get-go. Ascended Extra: In the 2003 cartoon, Silkie was a background character who occasionally had roles larger than cameos. In this series, he is featured more prominently and has several episodes that are focused on him. Badass Adorable: He has moments of this.

characters.name: Bumblebee
characters.description: Adaptational Superpower Change: In addition to her abilities maintained from the original series, Bumblebee also now has the ability to call and give orders to bees by whistling. Adaptational Wimp: While she still has the ability to fly and shrink, her B-shaped stingers from the original series used to zap people is replaced with bee-shaped guns to fire stingers. It’s still affective against foes, but not as much as before. Animal Motif: Of a bumblebee obviously. Ascended Extra: Originally a background character. Starting from "Forest Pirates", she joined the main cast for a temporary arc, becoming the Sixth Titan. Bee-Bee Gun: Bumblebee can use guns to fire bumblebee stingers. She can also use cannons to fire exploding beehives.

characters.name: King Shark
characters.description: Adaptational Heroism: The latest in several adaptations of King Shark to turn over a new leaf. Affably Evil: Although he is a villian, he's a pretty chill dude for the most part and is even willing to hang out with the Titans for a week. The Atoner: King Shark decides to temporarily join the Teen Titans to make up for eating Beast Boy and ruining their beach day. Big Eater: Being a half-shark, it’s natural for King Shark to have a big appetite. A Day in the Limelight: He is the main focus of "King Shark Week".

characters.name: Billy Numerous
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: In the original series, he suffered fromPower Incontinenceif he created too many clones and would weaken. Here he appears to be able to create clones without limit or any ill effect, to the point where on his day off he creates enough clones to fill up a stadium just to alleviate boredom. Adaptational Early Appearance: Billy Numerous was aSixth Rangerin the original series, who only joined the team during the last season, but here he's been on the team since the beginning. Eyes Out of Sight: His shades completely obscure his eyes, though they have been seen a few times whenever he gets burned. Me's a Crowd: His power is to create duplicates of himself at once, enough to play a game of baseball with just himself and his clones. Recurring Extra: He usually doesn't do anything except be there when the H.I.V.E. is there, clone himself and get beat up.

characters.name: Gizmo
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: While Gizmo is still evil, hisJerkasstendencies have been heavily toned down compared to the original series. Affably Evil: He's quite polite when he's not actively being a villain, and is very open in accepting new recruits into the H.I.V.E. Bald of Evil: Underneath his goggles, he’s completely bald. Crazy-Prepared: Has Kryptonite in his possession just in case Superman ever shows up; it's implied he's tangled with Superman before and chased him off with it as Superman doesn't mess with him. A Day in the Limelight: The episode "Villains in a Van Getting Gelato" focuses on Gizmo along with The Brain, Brother Blood and Dr. Light sharing stories about their bad experiences with the Titans.

characters.name: Jinx
characters.description: Adaptational Romance Downgrade: A romantic relationship between her and Kid Flash is pretty much non-existent in this series, although there is aMythology Gagin "Beast Man" showing the two in love on a magazine. Instead, her romantic partner in this series is Cyborg. Adaptational Villainy: Played with. While Jinx doesn't become a hero like her 2003 counterpart, she also acts as more of aIneffectual Sympathetic VillainandFriendly Enemy, rather than the straight-up bad guy she was pre-Heel–Face Turn. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: While she and Cyborg had a mutual attraction towards each other in the original series episode, "Deception", it ultimately doesn’t go anywhere due to Cyborg choosing to stay with the Titans instead of working for the H.I.V.E. Here, the two are upgraded to anOfficial Couplewho are able to date each other with no issue despite being in different alignments. Affably Evil: Jinx does a lot of stuff with her arch-enemies, like having a "Girls Night" which is her basically breaking stuff up and causing mayhem across the city, or in the case of his boyfriend Cyborg, have dates with him. Animal Eyes: She has cat-like eyes.

characters.name: Mammoth
characters.description: Adaptational Intelligence: In the original series, Mammoth was textbookDumb Muscle. In this show, he is depicted as having normal intelligence. The Brute: Serves as this for the H.I.V.E., being the physically strongest member. Butt-Monkey: In the episode "In and Out", the disguised Titans keep beating him up to prove their villain cred, even though each time Gizmo accepted them on the spot. Crossdresser: He dresses up as a ballerina for Halloween in "Scary Figure Dance". Evil Counterpart: To Beast Boy, as both of them serve as theBig Guyon the team.

characters.name: See-More
characters.description: Adaptational Early Appearance: See-More first appeared in the original show making a cameo in the season three premiere who only joined the team late in season four, but here he's been on the team since the beginning. Adaptational Romance Downgrade: See-More was shown to have a crush on Jinx in the original series. No such thing is seen or even implied with hisGo!incarnation. Beam-O-War: Frequently with Starfire. Cyber Cyclops: His helmet has a single robotic eye. Cyclops: He’s revealed to have one eye underneath his helmet.

characters.name: Blackfire
characters.description: Adaptational Late Appearance: Blackfire debuted in the second episode of the original series. In "Go!", she doesn't debut until the first episode of the second season. Adaptational Nice Guy: Unlike the original series, this version of Blackfire is portrayed much more sympathetically, as she sees the error of her ways and tried to repair her relationship with Starfire. Then Starfire got revenge and Blackfire went back to being evil. Her reappearance in "Girls' Night In" subverts this trope with a vengeance, as she is presented as one of the most serious threats the show has ever seen. Adaptation Dye-Job: In the 2003 series, Blackfire has a slightly tanned skin like compared to her sister and dark hair with purple accents. InGo!, she has paler skin, and her hair is also a lighter shade of purple. All Women Are Lustful: She isobsessed with Robin's buttand likes to constantly remark about it. Big Brother Bully: Well, Big Sister. To Starfire, initially.And later on.

characters.name: The Brain
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: In the original series, the Brain was aNon-Action Big Badand completely reliant on the assistant of others. Here he has access to a power suit that grants him arms and legs, while also possessing the ability to harnessstolen superpowers. Adaptational Comic Relief: The original Brain was aKnight of Cerebusand overall one of the nastiest threats the Titans had ever faced. Here he's as silly as every other character on the show. Adaptational Early Appearance: He was the finalArc Villainof the original show when it was in its final stages. Here, he appears in the second season ofGo!and isn't any sort ofFinal Bosscharacter. All Your Powers Combined: In "Brian" he steals all of the Titans' powers and uses them for his power suit. Ambiguously Gay: Implied to be in a relationship with Mallah.

characters.name: Brother Blood
characters.description: Adaptational Distillation: Aside from it being mentioned briefly in his introduction episode, his status as the headmaster of the H.I.V.E. Academy is never touched upon or discussed in this show. Adaptational Early Appearance: In the original series, Brother Blood appeared in the third season and ranked middle-of-the-road in terms of chronological appearance. InGo!, he appears very early on in the first season. Adaptational Wimp: Brother Blood lacks the fighting skills of his 2003 counterpart and his hypnotic powers are nowhere near as effective; with him needing to hook himself up to a machine in order to successfully hypnotize anyone. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: In the 2003 series, Brother Blood hadpersonal enmity with Cyborg the most. In this series, he seems to hate all the Teen Titans about equally and doesn't display any particular seething rage towards any one individual Titan over another. In fact, he states in "Villains in a Van Getting Gelato" that Beast Boy annoys him more than any other Titan. Ascended Extra: In the first show, Brother Blood was theArc Villainof the third season for Cyborg's character arc and doesn't make anymore appearances after that. InGo!, he's a recurring villain who isn't limited to a single season and has made sporadic appearances throughout the various seasons.

characters.name: Cinderblock
characters.description: Adaptational Wimp: Just to give you an idea, Robin took him down with a motorcycle. Let that sink in… Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: A giantRock Monsteron a rampage. Butt-Monkey: He is always injured. Dumb Muscle: He doesn't have much in the way of intelligence. Generic Doomsday Villain: No characterization outside of "mindless monster trying to destroy the city."

characters.name: Control Freak
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: In the previous series, he was barely a blip on the Titans' radar when it comes to their rogues. Here, he's aPhysical Godof aReality Warperthat made the universeDenser and Wackier. Likewise, while he was treated as aHarmless Villainin the previous series, he’s taken more seriously here, with Robin even outright calling him a monster for cancelling the previous series. Adaptational Romance Downgrade: It was implied in the original series episode "For Real" that he has a crush on Starfire, something that is nowhere to be seen inGo!. Adaptation Origin Connection: An interesting inversion, as most examples of this involve the villain being connected to the heroes' origin story. When Control Freak has his origin story explored in "Kyle", he's not the one who has a connection to the Titans' origin story,theyare the ones who are responsible forhisvillainStart of Darkness. Ascended Extra: In the first show, he was a minor, recurring villain who was never the biggest deal. In this series, he makes much more appearances as the central villain, is considered theGreater-Scope Villainwho got the 2003 series cancelled, has his origins explored in "Kyle", and gets his own major movie appearance inTeen Titans Go! & DC Super Hero Girls: Mayhem in the Multiverse. A Truce While We Gawk: Control Freak is apparently as much of aPretty Pretty Pegasusfan as Raven is, and the two take a moment in the middle of his battle with the Titans in "Friendship" to watch an episode on TV in a nearby television store and share their love for the show.

characters.name: Dr. Light
characters.description: Adaptational Heroism: On top of beingAffably Evilthis Dr Light made a legitimateHeel–Face Turnafter getting to know Starfire and Raven. The boys however proceed to ruin it and give him aHeel–Face Door-Slam. Affably Evil: He’s one of the friendlier villains in the series. He’s polite to Starfire and Raven while waiting for the rest of the Titans. He even pays for their meals when they had lunch together. He also wants to give up his life of crime and join the Titans until the boys beat him up and he is evil again because of them. In "Arthur", he has befriended all of the Titans (sans Robin) and they attempt to help him keep his job as the Titans' enemy when Robin threatens to fire him. Butt-Monkey: He is injured horribly in almost every episode he appears. Continuity Nod: In the post-Flashpoint version of the DC universe, Dr. Arthur Light was a good guy, so it makes sense that he's portrayed more sympathetically in this version. A Day in the Limelight: The episode "Villains in a Van Getting Gelato" focuses on Dr. Light along with Gizmo, brother Brain and Brother Blood sharing stories about their bad experiences with the Titans.

characters.name: Katarou
characters.description: Adaptation Dye-Job: Unlike the 2003 series, his outfit is maroon instead of black. Arch-Enemy: He’s one to Robin. Badass Normal: He was able to take the Titans down effortlessly with a few kicks and a butt attack. Bald of Evil: He is a villain with no hair. Cool Shades: Sports a pair while he describes himself to be cool.

characters.name: Killer Moth
characters.description: Adaptational Species Change: Downplayed. In the original show, he wasAmbiguously Human. Here, he's explicitly a mutant moth creature. His moth face even turns into a handsome human face when hit by his own mutation ray in "A Stickier Situation". Ambiguously Gay: "Robin's got it going on they all do". The Bus Came Back: Returns in Season 8 after having not appeared in four seasons. Early-Bird Cameo: Before his official debut in the show, he makes an appearance in the series’ tie in comics "Party, Party!" where he breaks into the tower to try and steal Silkie back from the Titans. Even Evil Has Loved Ones:He genuinely loves Silkie, and treats him like a child. He even put out a poster offering a large monetary reward for Silkie's return.He's also shown to care for his daughter, Kitten.

characters.name: Kitten
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: While still no threat at all, this Kitten is at least capable of doing villainous deeds without assistance from her father. Adaptational Romance Downgrade:Kitten hasn't shown any signs of being attracted to Robin in this series. She instead is seen dating Speedy, who in this series is basically Robin's doppelganger.In addition, Fang, her boyfriend from the original series, is ano-showin this series. Kitten hasn't shown any signs of being attracted to Robin in this series. She instead is seen dating Speedy, who in this series is basically Robin's doppelganger. In addition, Fang, her boyfriend from the original series, is ano-showin this series. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: In the original series, she was aDaddy's Little Villainto her father Killer Moth, with him doing villainous acts to cater to her every whim. InGo!, prior to Season 8, she never appeared with Killer Moth at all, with it not being established for years that they were even father and daughter.

characters.name: Kyd Wykkyd
characters.description: The Cameo: The only times he appear. Demoted to Extra: Due to not being with the H.I.V.E. in this series, he just appears as a background cameo character who has never gottenA Day in the Limelight. Expressive Mask: He looks very similar to Robin, even having a redExpressive Mask. Flat Character: Absolutely nothing is known about him in this series. Non-Member in the Adaptation: He was a member of the H.I.V.E. Five in the original series, but in this series he only makes a couple of cameos, and never appears with the H.I.V.E.

characters.name: Mad Mod
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: This Mad Mod succeeded in deaging the Titans and as of yet has not been defeated by them. Adaptational Late Appearance: Mad Mod first appeared in the original series in the ninth episode of the first season. Here, he doesn’t make his first appearance until season two. Art Evolution: These changes are minor, but with his reappearance in Season 9, Mad Mod has lost the black outlines around his eyes and his nose became slightly smaller. The Bad Guy Wins: Thanks to Raven, he succeeds in aging all of the Titans aside from her. British Teeth: His teeth are a bit unsightly and are notably the only aspect of his physical appearance tonotimprove after he starts draining people's youth to restore his own.

characters.name: Madame Rouge
characters.description: Adaptational Wimp: Zigzagged. She was a force to be reckoned with in the original show. While she was able to serve the Titans aCurb-Stomp Battleearlier in her debut episode, she was easily defeated by their gender-swapped counterparts, with a tail whip from Beast Girl's dinosaur form sending her flying. Adaptation Distillation: She was a member of the Brotherhood of Evil in the original show. Here, she shows no signs of being affiliated with either the Brain or Monsieur Mallah and appears on her very own in her debut episode. However, the tie-in comics based on the cartoon shows that she is indeed still affiliated with the Brotherhood. The Bus Came Back: After her debut, it took her four seasons to make another appearance as a cameo in "The Great Holiday Escape". Demoted to Extra: Only had one major role in the actual show despite being a more prominent villain in the original show for the duration of the fifth season. Early-Bird Cameo: Madame Rouge has appeared in several of the show's tie in comics before making her official debut in the TV series itself.

characters.name: Monsieur Mallah
characters.description: Adaptational Early Appearance: Like The Brain, he was the finalArc Villainof the 2003 show. Here, he appears in the second season ofGo! Adaptation Dye-Job: His fur is purple in "Go!" as opposed to black. Ambiguously Gay: Implied to be in a romantic relationship with The Brain. Ascended Extra: In previous appearances he was always a minor character with no lines. In "The Brain of the Family" Mallah finally plays a bigger role and gets to speak. Early-Bird Cameo: Before his debut in Season 2, The Brain makes an appearance in the series’ tie in comics "Idol Hands".

characters.name: Monster Cam
characters.description: Adaptational Species Change: In the original show, it was an unidentified monster whereas it’s a robot created by Control Freak in this show. Named In The Adaptation: The original series never gave it a name, simply being called referred to as the "White Monster" by fans. This series finally gives the White Monster an official name. The Voiceless: Just like in the original show.

characters.name: Mother Mae-Eye
characters.description: Adaptational Attractiveness: Her real form doesn't have warty green skin like she did in the original series. In fact herThird Eyeis the only inhuman feature. Adaptational Badass: Zigzagged. The original Mother Mae Eye was no slouch in battle, but seemed to prefer subtler long term methods such brainwashing to make her victims submissive. This Mother Mae Eye seems much more adept at direct hand-to-hand combat, and is overall more aggressive in her approaches in capturing her victims using hypnotism. Adaptational Early Appearance: She made her original series debut in the fourth season. Here, she makes her first appearance in the second episode of the series, being the first villain from the original show to reappear. Adaptational Jerkass: The original series Mother Mae Eye was eitherFaux Affably Evilor possibly evenObliviously Evilall the while she acted like a loving motherly figure. This version doesn't bother with such pleasantries and is much more openly hostile. Adaptational Superpower Change: The original Mother Mae Eye seemed to subtly induce a brainwashing trance, where her victims were lulled into a a blissful and childish stupor. This version of Mother Mae Eye utilizes more direct hypnosis that makes victims lose all cognitive awareness.

characters.name: Mumbo Jumbo
characters.description: Amazing Technicolour Population: Blue skin. Ambiguously Gay: Because he is a magician and is hammy which isCamp Gay. A Day in the Limelight: The episode "Christmas Magic" is about him sabotaging the Titans' Christmas. Evil Is Hammy: He acts like a real life magician. Harmless Villain: Subverted, he probably could put up a good fight, but he never gets a chance thanks to Raven'sStory-Breaker Power.

characters.name: No-Fu
characters.description: Adaptation Name Change: A subtle one. His species was called Newfu in the original series, while he referred to himself as the Source. Here a slight tweak of his species name has become his actual name. Hidden Villain: He is only revealed to be the mastermind at the very end of the episode. Non-Action Big Bad: As a sentient block of tofu, he has little in the way of combat and is quite defenseless against Beast Boy.

characters.name: Plasmus
characters.description: Adaptational Distillation: Unlike the original series, there's no traces of theTragic Villainwho would become ahumanoid slime monsterwhen he was conscious. Here he's just a mindless rampaging monster with no origin whatsoever. Adaptational Dumbass: Related to the above, this Plasmus' human side isAdapted Outso he no longer has any sentience. Adaptational Wimp: Zigzagged. He doesn’t seem to have any shape-shifting or stretching abilities like he did in the original show, but this incarnation is physically a lot stronger than the 2003 version. Blob Monster: What he is. Earth-Shattering Kaboom: In his first appearance, the Titans fail to stop him from blowing up a planet. How he survived being on a planet that was blown up is unknown.

characters.name: Punk Rocket
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He hasn’t made any appearance in the show since the third season. Dreadful Musician: Even without the destruction, his sound blasts are unbearable to most listeners. Flat Character: Not much can be said about his character in this show due to his limited screen presence. Instrument of Murder: His electric guitar produces sound blasts powerful enough to destroy buildings. Punny Name: OfPunk Rockof course.

characters.name: Ravager
characters.description: Abusive Parents: At the very least, she doesn't get along with her father and thinks he's lame. For those that don't know, her dad isSlade. Adaptational Villainy: In the comics, Rose was brainwashed by her father into becoming a villain. Here, she apparently became a villain of her own free will and actually thinks her father isn't evil enough. Age Lift: She seems older than the Titans rather than younger as her comics counterpart was. Ambiguously Gay: Rose's interactions with Raven often come across as flirtatious. She even looks at Raven with bedroom eyes on more than one occasion. Berserk Button: Trying to tell her what to do is a sure-fire way to piss Rose off.

characters.name: Slade
characters.description: Adaptational Badass:This Slade is far more impressive thananyother version of him, very nearly succeeding in world domination andmind controlover every superhero in the world.While the Slade of the original series made use ofSladebots, this Slade has upgraded to aHumongous Mecha. This Slade is far more impressive thananyother version of him, very nearly succeeding in world domination andmind controlover every superhero in the world. While the Slade of the original series made use ofSladebots, this Slade has upgraded to aHumongous Mecha. Adaptational Late Appearance: In the original series Slade was there from the start. In this series he doesn't debut until after three seasons, save for a few second cameo in "The Return of Slade". Adaptational Nice Guy: Compared to his 2003 counterpart, this Slade is substantially tamer, with his tendency to use torture and and mass-murder being scrubbed. This Slade is overall far more pragmatic. Even hisEvil Planto enslave the minds of everyone in the world, is painted in a depicted in a lighthearted and sillier tone.

characters.name: Terra
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy: In the previous series, she started out good, but was persuaded into villainy by Slade. In this series, she's evil from the start.Of course, compared to the original comic incarnation of Terra, this one is pretty much spot-on. Because You Were Nice to Me: She puts aside her obsession with revenge on the Titans after Raven admits that she actually thinks she's pretty cool. Judging from Terra's reaction to this remark, she's not used to such compliments from people and thus values them greatly. The Bus Came Back: She makes her first prominent appearance in over three years in "Girls Night In". Composite Character: Combines the scheming, hateful Terra from the comics with the more awkward, conflicted Terra from the show, making her a villain who enjoys being evil but still is capable ofPet the Dogmoments. Dark Action Girl: Unlike the original series, she starts off as being evil.

characters.name: Trigon
characters.description: Abusive Parents: Despite this Trigon being a much more loving father, he's still willing to fight his daughter Raven if she gets in his way, flicking her when he is giant in "The Titans Show", and uses a giant fist to crush her in "Thanksgiving". Adaptational Comic Relief: He's still evil and has plans on using Raven for hisEnd of the World as We Know Itschemes, but he's a lot more comical inGo!compared to the original show where he was played completely serious as aKnight of Cerebus. Adaptational Early Appearance: In the original show, he appeared late in the fourth season. Here, Trigon shows up early in the very first season of this show as Raven's recurringArchnemesis Dad. Adaptational Modesty: While his default outfit (consisting of only a belt and loincloth) is pretty much the same as the previous series, he does often don a more modest civilian attire in his more friendly moments with the Titans. Adaptational Nice Guy: In contrast to his usual portrayal as evil incarnate, this Trigon is portrayed as a loving,Bumbling Dadwho genuinely loves Raven and is more of aFriendly Enemyto the Titans. That said, he is still very much a villain, so Raven and the Titans still need to stop him every now and then.

characters.name: 50% Chad
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: He's one of the central characters in the "Starfire's Galaxy" mini-arc. Face–Heel Revolving Door: He accompanies Starfire to Tamaran to stop Blackfire from finding the Crown of King Fire despite also being a villain himself. Go-Karting with Bowser: As mentioned above, he accompanies Starfire on her space journey, as she deems him as "one of Earth's finest specimen." Half the Man He Used to Be: He's quite literally the lower half of a man. Though whether he ever had a top half or came into existence in his current state is unclear. Humanoid Abomination: He's simply just the bottom half of a larger being. How he's able to speak without a mouth is anyone's guess.

characters.name: Amanda Waller
characters.description: Adaptational Slimness: While most incarnations of Waller have her overweight, this one is slightly slimmer. Bad Boss: Disappoint her, and she'll blow your butt off (LITERALLY)! The Dreaded: The Titans fear her and try their absolute hardest to not disappoint herout of fear of getting their butts blown off. Sassy Black Woman: Courtesy of Roz Ryan.

characters.name: Balloon Man
characters.description: Adorable Evil Minions: His "kitties" balloons. At least, Starfire seems to to think so. Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: He's as big as a building, and very destructive. Curb-Stomp Battle: He is defeatedin literally two secondsby the Justice League. Help, I'm Stuck!: Subverted. He gets stuck between two buildings, but he quickly manages to free himself by inflating his body. Hurricane of Puns: He clearly likes to make lots of balloon-related puns.Balloon Man: Time to inflate my bank account!

characters.name: Beard Hunter
characters.description: Antagonist Title: His episode is titled after himself. "Not Making This Up" Disclaimer: The episode ends with Beast Boy remarking he can't believe the Beard Hunter is real, afterwards we see a recreation of the title page from the Beard Hunter's debut comic (Doom Patrolvolume two, issue 45) with a caption reading "THIS IS A REAL COMIC BOOK!"

characters.name: Black Manta
characters.description: Early-Bird Cameo: He makes a cameo in "Super Robin" in a framed photo before he makes his first appearance proper six seasons later.

characters.name: Captain Cold
characters.description: Early-Bird Cameo: Before debuting in the show proper, he’s made a few appearances in the tie-in comics and the mobile app games.

characters.name: Darkseid
characters.description: Adaptational Wimp: While Darkseid is normally depicted as giving the likes of Superman a run for his money, here, he's defeated relatively swiftly by Cyborg in his debut episode. It gets even worse in "The Streak" whereRobinis able to effortlessly beat him up. Arc Villain: He is the main villain of "Two-Parter". Early-Bird Cameo: He has made a number of cameos asEaster Eggsbefore officially appearing in person. Most notably as a plushie that sits on the side of the Titans' couch. Even Evil Has Standards: Zigzagged. Hewisheshe was "half as evil" as"Weird Al" Yankovicfor,in his perspective,"making songwriters look like fools"and earning money off of it. Evil Sounds Deep: Outright parodied. His deep, echoing, gravelly voice terrifies the Titans... and then it turns out he's just had a cold for a long time. One lozenge later,he turns into Weird Al.

characters.name: Doomsday
characters.description: Adaptational Intelligence: This Doomsday is fully sapient and capable of speech. While there have been some adaptations of Doomsday that are intelligent, usually he is depicted as a mindless beast of instinct. Badass Adorable: Doomsday maintains his standard appearance, buthis voice is that of a small childand claims that he just wants to have friends. Characterisation Marches On: In Doomsday's first appearance he has his standard mindless monster personality. However in his second appearance he has developed intelligence and now has the personality of a young child. Depending on the Artist: He will either be drawn with his standard evil appearance or with his much friendlier appearance first seen in "Doomsday Preppers". Evil All Along: After claiming thathe's just misunderstoodearly in the episode, it turns out in the end that Doomsday was planning to kill Superman from the start,though in Doomsday's defense, he had it coming.

characters.name: Gentleman Ghost
characters.description: Affably Evil: He's always extremely polite, though Starfire points out that this doesn't excuse his crimes. Baddie Flattery: He tells Raven that he finds her powers "impressive", hence why he decides to take possession of her body. Bank Robbery: He's in the middle of robbing a bank when the Titans comes to stop him. Deader than Dead: He's already a ghost, and he gets utterly destroyed by Raven's demonic powers. Demonic Possession: One of his powers is to take possession of other people's body.

characters.name: Rainbow Raider
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: Rainbow Raider is traditionally a C-Listjoke villainand consideredIn-Universeto be one of the most pathetic members of the Flash's Rogues. Here he is upgraded to the Flash's nemesis and has an additional power togo into paintingsthat makes him a great deal more difficult to deal with. Adaptational Superpower Change: In addition to hisHard Lightpowers, this version also has the power tocreate portals into paintings. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: This Rainbow Raider is upgraded to the Flash'sArch-Enemy, whereas he's usually one of Flash's more forgotten Rogues and never treated as any real threat. Arch-Enemy: This version is apparently the Flash's nemesis according to Starfire. The Bad Guy Wins: He ends his main episode actually defeating the Titans, after getting into good grace's with Starfire.

characters.name: Catwoman
characters.description: Adaptation Personality Change: This incarnation of Catwoman often behaves more like an actual cat than she does a human. Blonde, Brunette, Redhead: Harley is blonde, Catwoman is (likely) brunette, and Poison Ivy is redhead. A Day in the Limelight: "Jam" heavily focuses on the Gotham City Sirens recruiting Starfire and Raven for their roller derby team. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: In her earlier appearances, her mask hadMonochromatic Eyesand was thinner. Go-Karting with Bowser: The episode "Jam" has Starfire and Raven taking part in a roller derby on a team with Harley Quinn, Poison Ivy, and Catwoman.

characters.name: Egghead
characters.description: Bald of Evil: Due to his bald hair.

characters.name: Harley Quinn
characters.description: Blonde, Brunette, Redhead: Harley is blonde, Catwoman is (likely) brunette, and Poison Ivy is redhead. A Day in the Limelight: "Jam" heavily focuses on the Gotham City Sirens recruiting Starfire and Raven for their roller derby team. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: In her first physical appearance in "The Titans Show", she had her traditional jester design with the red and black jumpsuit which was later slightly tweaked in her cameo appearance inTeen Titans Go! To the Movies. Starting with "Jam", she has an appearance akin to how she appears inBirds of Prey (2020). Go-Karting with Bowser: The episode "Jam" has Starfire and Raven taking part in a roller derby team with Harley Quinn, Poison Ivy, and Catwoman. Red and Black and Evil All Over: She a villainess who wears a red and black jester jumpsuit.

characters.name: The Joker
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: A substantially nicer and sillier Joker than usual. While he does commit crimes, he can also be seen doing harmless activities and even hanging out with Batman and Commissioner Gordon on one occasion. Early-Bird Cameo: His first ever appearance was a brief cameo in "Real Boy Adventures", before later episodes had him featured in more plot important roles. Even before this initial appearance, he was alluded to several times in backgroundEaster Eggs. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: His first design had him withBlack Eyes of Insanity, which appears to be primarily based off his redesigned look fromThe New Batman Adventures. Later appearances give him more normal looking eyes. Go-Karting with Bowser: One episode has him hanging out with Batman and Commissioner Gordon, along with Penguin, sharing coffee together and laughing. Harmless Villain: To go along with Batman being goofier, this Joker is not the fearsome threat he usually is and is quite easy to defeat.

characters.name: Killer Croc
characters.description: Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Killer Croc has had three different designs throughout the series. His first few appearances has him completely covered in cyan scales. His second design seen in "The Inner Beauty of a Cactus" has him more green than cyan, his scales are also much more defined, he’s bony protrusions stick out from the top of his skull all the way down his spine, and has a much more bulkier appearance overall. His current design is similar to his second one, but with a muscular build akin to his first design. Go-Karting with Bowser: He has no problem with letting Batman and Commissioner Gordon watching under-the-sea TV with him in "TV Knight 4". Rogues' Gallery Transplant: Zigzagged. While Killer Croc is traditionally one of Batman's adversaries, he has also crossed paths with the Teen Titans multiple times. Strangely, in "The Titans Show" he is shown among the Titans' villains watching their island adventures instead of with the mainstream DC villains at the end of the episode. The Voiceless: He doesn’t talk.

characters.name: Poison Ivy
characters.description: Blonde, Brunette, Redhead: Harley is blonde, Catwoman is (likely) brunette, and Poison Ivy is redhead. A Day in the Limelight: "Jam" heavily focuses on the Gotham City Sirens recruiting Starfire and Raven for their roller derby team. Go-Karting with Bowser: The episode "Jam" has Starfire and Raven taking part in a roller derby team with Harley Quinn, Poison Ivy, and Catwoman. Suddenly Speaking: Speaks for the first time in "Jam" after making several non-speaking appearances.

characters.name: The Riddler
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Unlike most of the other villains in Batman's rouge gallery, he hasn't made any appearances in the later seasons, with his latest appearance being in "Mo' Money, Mo' Problems" in Season 4. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: in his first few appearance, his face would be at aCheated Anglewith a pointy nose. The Voiceless: One of the many characters who never gets to speak.

characters.name: Sofia Falcone
characters.description: Rogues' Gallery Transplant: A member of Batman's rogues gallery who goes up against the Titans a few times.

characters.name: Two-Face
characters.description: Early Installment Character-Design Difference: His first appearance in "The Titans Show" is based heavily off of his appearance inBatman: The Animated Series. The Voiceless: He doesn’t have a speaking role as of yet.

characters.name: Easter Bunny
characters.description: Anti-Hero: Technically, he's not actually bad at all - but he's not someone you'd want to be friends with. Creepy Good: Lovingly lays eggs for all the people of the world to enjoy. Also likes to watch people eat said eggs. However,no onewants the eggs as they find both him and his ability to lay them disgusting. He Cleans Up Nicely: Somehow a makeover transforms him into a human hunk, albeit with bunny ears. Mister Seahorse: If his ability to lay eggs didn't already count him as such, his child with the Tooth Fairy hatches from one at the end of "Eater Creeps." Token Good Teammate: Pretty much the only holiday mascot on the show who isn't secretly evil. He's creepy, but never actually mean. Hell, the one time he even stood up for himself ended with him falling in love with the target.

characters.name: Ed
characters.description: Chekhov's Gunman:Cameos for about a secondin "Pie Bros" before playing a major role in the next episode, "Driver's Ed". He then makes two more cameos after that episode, despite going to Hell in it. Devil in Plain Sight: It's apparent to everyone that he's a bank robber, except Robin. Until it's revealed, Robin knew all along, but cared more about getting his licence. Four Eyes, Zero Soul: A bespectacled bank robber. Obviously Evil: To everyone. Even Robin. Sadist Teacher: A driving instructor who uses giving permit tests as a cover up for having a getaway driver.

characters.name: Evil Dragon
characters.description: Big Bad: Of "The Day the Night Stopped Beginning to Shine and Became Dark Even Though it Was the Day". In Their Own Image: The dragon wants to destroy the song in order to darken the world of The Night Begins To Shine and rule it as its king once more. Knight of Cerebus: He's taken seriously since he has a desire to wipe out free will by destroying music.

characters.name: Flex
characters.description: Resemblace: Chuck in theAngry Birdsseries.

characters.name: Muscle
characters.description: Resemblace: Red in theAngry Birdsseries.

characters.name: Pain Bot
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: It exists solely to cause pain. Broken Record: "Pain. Pain. Pain.""All I know is pain. All I know is pain." "All I know is pain. All I know is pain." Cute Machines: Cyborg sure thinks so. Heel–Face Turn: Cyborg adopts it once Brother Blood's remote control is destroyed. This does not meaningfully reduce its aggression in the least, at least to the other Titans. Its attacks on Cyborg become much milder, to the point where Cyborg sees them as Pain Bot's way of licking him like an affectionate puppy.

characters.name: Santa Claus
characters.description: Bad Santa: Santa is portrayed as a hateful, spiteful, disgusting, and crude old man, who also has villainous tendencies and has made many attempts to destroy the Teen Titans, being probably the most recurring villain of this show who's not a comic books or 2003 series rogue.Santa: Garbage children. Catchphrase: "Garbage children." Child Hater: His tendency to say "garbage children" suggests he doesn't have a favorable opinion on kids. Friendly Enemy: Despite trying to kill them every Christmas, Santa assists Robin and Beast Boy in beating Kid Flash in "The Streak", by joining their team and giving Robin a lesson in leadership. Leitmotif: "Allhailthe jolly fat man!"

characters.name: Tooth Fairy
characters.description: Heel–Face Revolving Door: Whether she's an ally to the Titans or their enemy depends on the episode. Karma Houdini: Her attempt to take over Easter and steal people's teeth ends in her getting a husband. Vocal Dissonance: Has a male voice, but "Easter Creeps" confirms she's female.

characters.name: Ultralak
characters.description: Big Bad: Of "The Night Begins to Shine 2: You're The One". Knight of Cerebus: He's taken very seriously and is possibly the darkest villain in the show. Vile Villain, Saccharine Show: In a show where even formerly dark 2003Teen Titansvillains like Slade and Trigon are given more comedic traits, Ultralak especially stands out as being one of the darker and more serious villains in a lighter-hearted series that skews to a younger demographic. With Great Power Comes Great Insanity: Ultralak was once the rhythm guitarist of B.E.R. only to become mad with power once he was consumed by it. After being isolated and left alone, he became a tyrant and set out to destroy all music and rule the universe in dark silence.

characters.name: Carlos
characters.description: Cane Sword: Pulls one out on Silkie. Disney Villain Death: Silkietricks him into charging off a balcony and down a cliff.He's later shown hanging from a branchand gets grabbed by a giant hawk. Fat Bastard: He's a bit portly and considerably mean. Green-Eyed Monster: Was jealous that his ex-girlfriend is dating Silkie. He goes as far as to kidnap them and lock them in his mansion. Jerkass: He is extremely controlling of his ex girlfriend. He even locks her and Silkie up.

characters.name: Death
characters.description: Even Evil Has Loved Ones: He seems to be fond of Raven. However, it doesn't mean that he'd give up the Titans' souls for her. Evil Uncle: He refers to himself as Raven's uncle. However, it is unknown if he actually is related or if he's just a close acquaintance of Trigon and therefore Raven'sHonorary Uncle. Grim Reaper: The personification of it. Large Ham: He screams a lot. Villain Song: His "Last Breath" Song counts as this.

characters.name: Scary Teri
characters.description: All Myths Are True: Much to the surprise of everybody, sans Cyborg. I'm a Humanitarian: Eats Beast Boy, Raven, Starfire, and Robin. Voluntary Shapeshifting: Does this several times. Wicked Witch: Cyborg calls her one although it is unclear if this is literal or an insult. It could also be aMythology Gag.noteAs Bloody Mary is often said to be a witch's ghost.

characters.name: Twin Destroyers of Azarath
characters.description: The Antichrist: They exist to destroy the world. Eldritch Abomination: They're demons who feed offThe Power of Love, which causes them to fuse together into a two-headed world destroying monster. The Power of Love: They literally feed off it. Ridiculously Cute Critter: Irresistibly cute.

characters.name: Hurt Bot
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: Like Pain Bot, it exists solely to inflict pain (or hurt in this case) Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Despite being Pain Bot’s replacement for Brother Blood, "The Best Robin” is its only appearance in the show and hasn’t been seen or mentioned again since. It’s possible that Brother Blood never bothered to rebuild it after it was destroyed by the Super Robin. Convenient Replacement Character: Is this to Pain Bot’s. Once Pain Bot pulls aHeel–Face Turnand becomes Cyborg's little buddy, Brother Blood builds Hurt Bot as a replacement. Pokémon Speak: "Hurt". Replacement Goldfish: Pain Bot’s replacement for Brother Blood after the former pulls aHeel–Face Turnand became an ally of the Titans.

characters.name: Grizzly Bear
characters.description: Animal Nemesis: Constantly menaces Beast Boy while he is living in the wilderness.

characters.name: Honk
characters.description: Expy: A very deliberate pastiche of the Joker where he was made to be aReplacement Goldfishto Slade by becoming an evilMonster Clown. Monster Clown: Beast Boy and Cyborg turn him into one.

characters.name: Parry
characters.description: A giant monster from another planet who pretended to be Starfire's friend. Is eventually revealed to be the cyronelian chrysalis eater fromTeen Titans. Adaptational Abomination: The original series Cyronelian Chrysalis Eater was a more simple shapeshifter with two forms, this one burrows under Starfire's skin like a parasite and can telepathically communicate. Canon Character All Along: It originally seemed like another one of the show's bizarre original characters, but turns out to be the Cyronelian Chrysalis Eater from the original series. Evil All Along:Robinspends the whole episode being untrusting of Parry to the disbelief of the other Titans, before a private conversation with Parry finally swayed him. Turns out in the endRobin was right all alongwith Parry revealing its true form as the Cyronelian Chrysalis Eater who proceeds to crush the Titans. Manipulative Bastard: Manages to deceive Starfire and the rest of the Titans (Robinin particular) into believing it to be a benign creature, until it is finally ready to strike.

characters.name: Puppet Wizard
characters.description: Art Shift: He is depicted in live-action. Demonic Dummy: A demonic sockpuppet to be precise. Expy: Seems to be a stand-in for the Puppet King from the 2003 series.

characters.name: Sandwich Guardians
characters.description: Starter Villain: They're the first villains fought in the first episode ofTeen Titans Go!

characters.name: Klatak
characters.description: Amazing Technicolor Population: She has pink skin.

characters.name: King Goal
characters.description: All Trolls Are Different: He is a pink/purple troll. Fat Bastard: He's a very obese villain. Giant Mook: He is larger than the Soccer Trolls. King Mook: Of the Soccer Trolls. Non-Humans Lack Attributes: He wears no clothes, but has no visible genitals.

characters.name: Bizarro Titans
characters.description: Affably Evil: In contrast to their evil counterparts, the Titans, the Bizarro Titans are more cordial and well-mannered. Bad Is Good and Good Is Bad: Due to being Bizarros, they say the opposite of what they really mean, which leads to Grobyc, Boy Beast, Nevar and Erifrats interpreting Robin's compliments as insults. Evil Counterpart: Or in this case, Good Counterpart, to the Teen Titans. Punch-Clock Villains: They are only villains when not hanging around at home doing whatever they feel like. Sdrawkcab Name: Most of their names are just the names of their regular counterparts spelled backwards (e.g. Nibor for Robin, Erifrats for Starfire) rather than the character's regular name with "Bizarro" in front of it like the traditional naming conventions for Bizarro duplicates. The one exception is Beast Boy's Bizarro World counterpart, who is named Boy Beast.

characters.name: Dr. Military
characters.description: Face–Heel Turn: At some point, he was the vetrinarian for Jump City's police dogs. Foul Waterfowl: To pay off his med school loans, he stole a bunch of ducks from a wildlife refuge and turned them into an army. Lantern Jaw of Justice: Inverted, due to his being a bad guy and all that. Remember the New Guy?: He's introduced as if he's appeared before, but exactly when was never shown.

characters.name: In general
characters.description: Adaptational Relationship Overhaul: Their relationship with the core Teen Titans team appears to be a rivalry rather than the comradeship they had with them in the 2003 series. Always Someone Better: Zigzagged. The Titans East have been shown to be more competent than the Teen Titans on several occasions. For example, as revealed in "Forest Pirates", they are one of the teams to always win the annual canoe race at summer camp. However, with that being said, the Titans have managed to make it further than them in the "Justice League Top Talent Idol Star" competitions and beat them in Crime Season every year. Ambiguous Situation: There has never been a definitive answer on who the leader of the team is supposed to be in this continuity, since the show seems to fluctuate on who it is from episode to episode. Kid Flash is implied to be the leader of his team of Titans formed in "Flashback", while Aqualad is implied to be the leader in several other episodes, while he and Speedy are implied to both be leaders in "We're Off To Get Awards". Finally, Bumblebee is implied to be the leader in both "The Viewers Decide" and "DC Leader Swap". The only time the leader of the team has been mentioned is in theTeeny Titansapp game where it’s stated that Bumblebee is the leader like in the 2003 series, and even that should be taken with a grain of salt depending on whether or not the game is actually canon to the TV series. A Day in the Limelight: They have prominent appearances in "Flashback" and "The Viewers Decide". Living Prop: More often than not, they would make background appearances with no barring to the plot.

characters.name: Aqualad
characters.description: Adaptational Jerkass: This Aqualad doesn't often care for the wellbeing of his marine friends except for some shrimp and “Mr. Belvedere”, and seems to view them as expendable tools. Anti-Villain: Despite being a superhero, he often shows antagonistic traits in this show. Whether it be misusing the marine life, keeping Berto hostage for cooking shrimps, and even tries to kill Beast Boy and Raven for trying to sabotage he and Terra’s relationship in "Rocks and Water". The Beastmaster: Much like the original series he has full control over marine life, but unlike the original series he treats them like slaves. Butt-Monkey: Beast Boy is always harassing him just because he likes Raven. The Casanova: In this series, not only is he aChick Magnet, but he also acts like he owns every girl who is attracted to him.

characters.name: Kid Flash
characters.description: The Ace: Robin accuses him of being a "one trick pony", due to only having his speed, but it turns out due to his speed allowing him to learn quickly he is able to rapidly amass as many talents as Robin has. Adaptational Early Appearance: Kid Flash first appeared in the original show's fifth and final season. Here, he makes his first appearance in Season 2. Adaptational Jerkass: Kid Flash is presented as more antagonistic and egotistical in this show. Adaptational Romance Downgrade: A romantic relationship between him and Jinx is pretty much non-existent in this series, although there is aMythology Gagin "Beast Man" showing the two in love on a magazine. When taking her down in his debut episode, however, he simply knocks her over with his hip with a somewhat flirtatious look on his face, implying that his feelings for her are still there. Always Second Best: Robin always finds himself overshadowed by Kid Flash at everything.

characters.name: Más y Menos
characters.description: Adaptational Dye-Job: They have pink hair as opposed to red-orange hair like in the original show. Adaptational Early Appearance: They debuted in the tail end of Season 3 of the original show, while in this series they debut early Season 1. Adaptational Intelligence: The twins appear to be wiser and more intelligent here than in the 2003 series, astheyare the ones to teach the Titans lessons such as trying new things and working together. A Day in the Limelight: Both of them in “Mas y Menos”. Divergent Character Evolution: It’s a minor detail, but Menos is given a bigger gap in his teeth compared to Más.

characters.name: Speedy
characters.description: Adaptational Early Appearance: Speedy debuts in the show 6 episodes in, while it took him until late Season 2 to appear in the 2003 series. Adaptational Relationship Overhaul:In the original 2003 series, he and Robin got along pretty well and they had more of a friendly rivalry. In this series, the two of them have a bitter rivalry with each other with no signs of cordiality.In this show, Speedy has shown a romantic interest in both Starfire and Kitten, neither of whom he’s had any interactions with in the original cartoon. In the original 2003 series, he and Robin got along pretty well and they had more of a friendly rivalry. In this series, the two of them have a bitter rivalry with each other with no signs of cordiality. In this show, Speedy has shown a romantic interest in both Starfire and Kitten, neither of whom he’s had any interactions with in the original cartoon. Adaptational Wimp: A fair bit more weaker than the usual Speedy. Considering Robin was able to take him down twice, when they were evenly matched in the original series, especially taking into account this version of Robin's ownincreased wimp factors.

characters.name: Batgirl
characters.description: Adaptational Dye-Job: Usually a red head, here it's more orange. Bound and Gagged: After being captured by Dick Gravestone (Robin) in "Snuggle Time". The Cameo: Like Batman, but not as often. She's shown up as a cameo more often than other characters on this list though. A Day in the Limelight: In “Staring at the Future”. Happily Married: She becomes this toNightwing in "Staring at the Future".

characters.name: Batman
characters.description: Abusive Parents: To some extent. Robin, who is technically Batman's adopted son, is absolutely terrified of Batman because he apparently punishes Robin corporeally. Adaptational Comic Relief: This version of Batman is far more laid-back and jokey than his usual dark, brooding self. This is given a lampshade in "Real Orangins" when the Titans refuse to believe Robin's story involving a grim, gritty Batman when the one in their show is right by them cackling away with Gordon. Ascended Extra: He was merely aRunning Gagcharacter early on in the series where he would make a few quick gag appearances every now and then. He becomes a much more prominent character later on in the show, going on to have several supporting roles and even starring inhis own series of episodes. The Cameo: Both in pictures on the walls in Titans Tower, among other things, and has made a few quick gag appearances in person. Comically Serious: If he's not in the background with Commissioner Gordon, Batman will likely show up and silently glare contrasting with the silliness of everyone else.

characters.name: Alfred Pennyworth
characters.description: Art Evolution: He is drawn with a much more muscular build in the movie compared to his previous appearances in the show, although he goes right back to his normal slim build right afterwards. Badass Normal: Despite being a mere butler, he's certainly no slouch when it comes to hand-to-hand combat, as he was able to take down many of Batman's enemies in "Mo' Money Mo' Problems". Battle Butler: He saved the Wayne Manor from getting robbed by Batman's rogue gallery by easily defeating the villains with his butler styled combat skills. A Day in the Limelight: He’s somewhat of an antagonist in the "TV Knight" series of episodes where he would be the obstacle preventing Batman from watching TV, either unintentionally or purposefully. Papa Wolf: He’s real protective towards his master.

characters.name: The Chief
characters.description: Abusive Parents: He surgically transplants his oldest adoptive son's brain into a robot body and permanently transforms his adoptive daughter into a negative energy being, which his children only consented to due to being offered solutions to their problems and not fully knowing what they were agreeing to. Adaptation Dye-Job: Traditionally depicted with either red hair or gray hair in the comics, this version of Niles Caulder instead has white hair. Composite Character: In an inverse of Mento taking his role as the Doom Patrol's leader in the 2003 cartoon, this continuity has the Chief take Mento's role as Beast Boy's adoptive father. Genius Cripple: He's intelligent and wheelchair-bound. Heroic Comedic Sociopath: He made Robotman and Negative Girl what they are now to help them with their problems and excuses the drastic measures of putting Cliff's brain in a robot body and transforming Negative Girl into a negative energy being under the grounds that it wouldn't have been as fun as just teaching Cliff to dance better and sharing his arcade tickets with Negative Girl. It's obvious he just wanted an excuse to irreversibly change his adoptive children's bodies and it's played entirely for humor.

characters.name: Elasti-Girl
characters.description: Hartman Hips: She’s drawn with incredibly wide hips. Mama Bear: She’s very protective of her adopted children. Race Lift: This incarnation of Rita Farr is black rather than Caucasian. Related in the Adaptation: Because Robotman and Negative Girl are Beast Boy's adoptive siblings in this continuity, she is by extension Robotman and Negative Girl's adoptive mother as well as Beast Boy's.

characters.name: Robotman
characters.description: Adaptational Backstory Change: Instead of his brain being put into a robot body by the Chief after his original body was mangled in an accident (which was later revealed to have been arranged by the Chief in the first place), this version of Cliff Steele apparently had his brain transplanted into a robot body in order to beat a rival at a dance competition, the Chief feeling that doing so is cooler than simply teaching Cliff better dance moves. Adaptational Nationality: This version of Cliff Steele is German. Related in the Adaptation: He is the Chief's oldest adoptive son as well as Beast Boy and Negative Girl's adoptive brother.

characters.name: Negative Girl
characters.description: Adaptational Backstory Change: Larry Trainor became Negative Man when an accident caused his body to become radioactive (requiring him to wear chemically-treated bandages for everyone else's protection) and gave him the power to have an energy being fly out of his body to act on his behalf. Negative Girl instead became how she is when the Chief used a ray to turn her into a negative energy being just so she could use her powers to beat an arcade game and win enough tickets to get a teddy bear she wanted. Age Lift: While Larry Trainor and Valentina Vostok were adults, Negative Girl is but a child in this continuity. Gender Flip: If she's not a de-aged Valentina Vostok, then she's a de-aged and female Larry Trainor. Lighter and Softer: Instead of dying, the consequences of Negative Girl's energy self staying outside of her body too long is that she'llwet herself. Related in the Adaptation: She is the Chief's adoptive daughter as well as Beast Boy and Robotman's adoptive sister.

characters.name: B'wana Beast
characters.description: Fusion Dance: He can fuse any two animals together. His demonstration with Silkie and a rabbit led to him being rejected from joining the Titans. Loincloth: Cyborg makes fun of him for wearing a loincloth. Recurring Extra: Mostly appears in the background with not too much focus. Top-Heavy Guy: Like most of the "muscular" characters on this show, his legs are spindly compared to his huge upper body. Unfortunate Names: Cyborg keeps on making fun of his name during his audition.

characters.name: Detective Chimp
characters.description: The Cameo: In the movie. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: When he first appears in "You're Fired", he wears a different looking hat and no clothes. Talking Animal: As per usual, he's an ape who can talk.

characters.name: Robins
characters.description: Always Someone Better: All of them seem to do better than the main Robin, much to his dismay. No Name Given: As with the other heroes in the series, their secret identities aren't revealed. But two of them resemble Tim Drake and Carrie Kelly, while the third resembles the Golden/Silver Age Robin (Dick Grayson). Possibly averted, as recent CN promos actually call the former two Tim Drake and Carrie Kelly. Classic Robin is still just called Classic Robin though. Hemaybe meant to represent a Pre-Crisis Jason Todd, but it's not entirely clear. One-Steve Limit: Hilariously averted. They're all called Robin, even by the other Robins. Ambiguous Situation: He's either the past self of Dick Grayson (the show's main Robin), or aLighter and SofterJason Todd. It's not quite clear which. Camp Straight: He has a more flamboyant attitude than the other Robins.

characters.name: Vixen
characters.description: Animal Eyes: Has orange eyes with cat-like pupils. My Instincts Are Showing: Would've been on the Titans, but she ate a worm while using the powers of an eagle and was rejected. Power Copying: Can copy the traits of any nearby animal. Recurring Extra: She mostly just appears as a background character with not too much focus. The Voiceless: The only sound she makes during her appearance was an eagle squawk.

characters.name: Wonder Twins
characters.description: Adapted Out: They usually appear with their pet monkey, Gleek, but he goes unseen and unmentioned inGo! The Bus Came Back: They make their first major appearance in "Activate" after 12 years of being non-speaking background characters. Butt-Monkey: While Jayna fights crime with the Titans, Zan gets stuck as a receptionist. He was only let on the team because Jayna needs him to use her powers. Half-Identical Twins: The only differences between them are their voices, their genders, and their physiques. Leotard of Power: Both of them wear one.

characters.name: Young Justice
characters.description: Adapted Out: This version of Young Justice doesn’t include Robin, Kid Flash, Artemis or Zatanna. Justified in Robin and Kid Flash's case, since they are already pre-existing characters in theTeen Titansfranchise and are instead members of the Teen Titans. Artemis and Zatanna, however, would make appearances in future episodes, although whether they’re associated with Young Justice or not is unknown. Art Evolution: They later appear in themoviewith new designs that fit theTeen Titans Go!artstyle. Art Shift: Kaldur, Superboy, and Miss Martian retain their designs fromYoung Justice (2010), just losing out on all the shading they had. Gone Horribly Right: Their discussion with the Titans to tell them to get more serious results with the Titans getting so serious that they end up getting dangerously destructive during one mission, and later they end up disbanding due to gettingsoserious that they get into a massive fight over a juice box, albeit temporarily thanks toStatus Quo Is God. Mythology Gag:Although Speedy and Kid Flash aren't members of the team in this version, they do associate with them in the summer camp arc, in addition to a reference to Artemis and Wally's romantic relationship in a Valentine's Day episode.The hostility between them and Robin is likely a reference to how Robin was one of the founding members and a leader of Young Justice, especially in the television show.

characters.name: Aquaman
characters.description: Adaptational Jerkass: In "Finding Aquaman", he abandons the Titans to die in quite an un-heroic fashion. Chick Magnet: To the point where Starfire doesn't mind being paired with him in "Matched". She does admire his physique. A Day in the Limelight: Ordinarily appears only in cameos, but has a bigger role in the movie and "Justice Leagues Next Top Talent Idol Star". He then goes on to star in "Finding Aquaman" and "Pool Season". Uncertain Doom: Towards the end of "Finding Aquaman", the Titans wonder where Aquaman could be. Black Manta's cat then spits out Aquaman's shrunken trident, implying he got eaten but a body isn't shown either way.

characters.name: Commisioner Gordon
characters.description: Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Much like with Batman, Commissioner Gordon has had three different designs throughout the series. His debut featured him with a lankier appearance while his remaining Season 1 appearances have him with a round build. He underwent his final design seen for the rest of the series in Season 2, making him more muscular in appearance. Heroes Gone Fishing: He is frequently seen hanging out and goofing off with Batman. Heterosexual Life-Partners: With Batman. The Hyena: Alongside Batman, he laughs a lot. Recurring Extra: Mainly just appears as a background character.

characters.name: Green Lantern (John Stewart)
characters.description: Ascended Extra: He initially shows up in a few silent cameos, but doesn't get an actual speaking role untilthe movie. A Day in the Limelight: After several initial cameos, as a more important role in the movie and "Two Parter". Early Installment Character-Design Difference: In his very first appearance, GL resembled hisJustice League Unlimitedincarnation, right down the goatee and bald head. All subsequent appearances have instead used his standard clean shaven appearance from the comics. Let Us Never Speak of This Again: He's embarrassed byGreen Lantern (2011), a notoriousBox-Office Bomb. He wasn't eveninthat movie, but apparently Hal Jordan ended up embarrassing theentire Green Lantern Corpswith its creation. Troll: The ending of "Orangins" reveals thatBeast Boy isn't actually real, and is just a construct made by John's Green Lantern Ring in order to prank the Titans.

characters.name: Superman
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy: He ends up as the main antagonist of the episode, "Four Hundred", where he purposefully banishes the Titans to the stop-motion dimension for winning the award for "DC's longest animated show". Casting Gag: He's voiced in the film by Nic Cage, which is meant as a nod toTim Burton's ill-fatedSuperman Livesmovie, which would have starred Cage as the title character. A Day in the Limelight: After several cameos, has a larger role in the movie, "TV Knight 3", "Two Parter", "Justice Leagues Next Top Talent Idol Star" and "Four Hundred". Disproportionate Retribution: He banishes the Titans to the Stop-Motion Dimension in "Four Hundred" for winning the award for "DC's longest animated show" instead of the Justice League.

characters.name: Wonder Woman
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Like Green Lantern, her first actual speaking role comes in the movie, where she has a more significant part than usual. She’s gotten many more appearances in the series since then. Costume Evolution: After initially appearing in her classic outfit in the series, the movie gave Wonder Woman her outfit from the 2017 Wonder Woman film, which has been kept in later episodes of the show. A Day in the Limelight: After several cameos, she has a larger role in the movie, "TV Knight 3", "Two Parter", and "Justice Leagues Next Top Talent Idol Star". Older Than She Looks: "DC" reveals that Wonder Woman is actually 80 years old.

characters.name: The Flash
characters.description: Mythology Gag: His appearance seems to be based off of his costume inThe Flash (2014).

characters.name: Martian Manhunter
characters.description: Mythology Gag: His appearance is based off of his design in theJustice Leaguecartoon. Meanwhile, his appearance in the mobile game is based off of his design in theYoung Justice (2010)cartoon.

characters.name: The Atom
characters.description: Amusing Injuries: Upon arriving at Batman's movie premiere, he is promptly stepped on by Robin, who barely gives it a second thought. The next we see of him, he's covered in bruises and bandages and even missing a few teeth.

characters.name: Hawkman
characters.description: Speaks Fluent Animal: True to his name, he usually makes hawk sounds. Suddenly Speaking: After several non-speaking appearances, he speaks for the first time in "Winged Warriors".

characters.name: Black Canary
characters.description: Adaptational Romance Downgrade: Despite her relationship with Green Arrow in the mainstream DC comics, their romance is never touched on or even alluded to in this series, so one would wonder whether or not they’re even an item in this canon to begin with. Ambiguously Bi: She is canonically in a relationship with Green Arrow in the mainstream comics. However, she seemed to have no issue being romantically paired with Elasti-Girl in "Manors and Mannerisms". A Day in the Limelight: She is revealed to be a member of the Winged Warriors in the episode of the same name. Suddenly Speaking: Finally gets a speaking role in "Winged Warriors" after several seasons of making non-speaking appearances.

characters.name: Wonder Girl
characters.description: Adaptational Relationship Overhaul: Donna having a romantic interest in Robin is a complete contrast to the comics, in which they are shown as having a strong platonic brother/sister like relationship. Age-Gap Romance: Implied with her ex-boyfriend being a lumberjack, who appears to look much older than her. Starfire also pairs her with the Flash in "Manor and Mannerisms". Ascended Extra: Due to licensing and legal issues, Wonder Girl only appeared in non-physical cameos in the original show, without ever making a full appearance (outside of the tie-in comics). However, since those issues have since been lifted, she makes a more prominent appearance inTeen Titans Go!as a recurring character. Bait-and-Switch: During her appearance inThe Bergerac, she tells Robin she already has a boyfriend... who turns out to be a lumberjack instead of a Green Lantern. But Now I Must Go: After Robin and Wonder Girl share a kiss, she decides to leave camp and to never see Robin again since camp romances never last. She even tells him that he can't even text or call her.

characters.name: The Monitor
characters.description: Rage Breaking Point: He slowly becomes annoyed when the Titans keep messing up in their simulations of their past adventures, finally deciding enough is enough when they reveal that they intentionally hold back so Robin can, in his words, "feel useful". So Proud of You: He becomes happy to find the Titans have learned their lesson, even showing this same happiness when they decide to beat him up. The Only Way They Will Learn: Takes this approach when the Titans reveal that they intentionally hold back on their powers for Robin's sake Trickster Mentor: He puts the Titans into a simulation where they have no powers an Robin seemingly dies, then reveals the ruse when the Titans show regret about not using their powers properly.

characters.name: Vibe
characters.description: Cool Shades: Sports a pair straight from the 80s. Dance Battler: He uses breakdancing moves as part of his fighting style. Early-Bird Cameo: Before appearing in the flesh in "Justice League's Next Top Talent Idol Star: Dance Crew Edition", Robin is given his powers in "My Name Is Jose" and he even makes a cameo in an imagination spot. Living Prop: Like other assorted DC heroes in the show, he normally just says and does nothing in the background. Recurring Extra: One of the many in the show.

characters.name: Blue Beetle and Booster Gold
characters.description: Adaptational Sexuality: These incarnations of Blue Beetle and Booster Gold are stated to be a couple, when in the comics Booster Gold has a biological son in Rip Hunter through an unidentified mother and he and Blue Beetle wereHeterosexual Life-Partnerswho at one pointreacted negatively to being assumed that they are gay. Blue Is Heroic: Blue Beetle wears a blue super suit. Is that really a surprise? Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: Booster Gold is a superhero with golden hair. Living Prop: What most of their appearances amount to. Official Couple:Word of Godconfirms that they are dating in the show.

characters.name: Powerpuff Girls
characters.description: Action Girl: Well theyarethe Powerpuff Girls. Badass Adorable: Young children with superpowers. Color-Coded for Your Convenience: Blossom is Red, Bubbles is Blue, and Buttercup is Green. Foil: To the Titans, being heroes who actually care about fighting crime unlike the incompetent Titans who mess around. Specifically each girl has a Titans counterpart. Bubbles to Starfire (ditzy nice girl), Blossom to Robin (Control Freakleader), Buttercup to Raven (tomboyish tough girl). Good Versus Good: The entire premise of the crossover. Though it's more of a case ofWhite-and-Grey Moralityconsidering the Titans are barely heroes.

characters.name: Birdarang
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Went from being an one-time gag from "Power Moves" to one of the most frequently appearing side characters. Beware the Nice Ones: He’s not always one who gets mad, but he’s pretty good at fighting. Catchphrase: "That's Ridonculous", "Word!" Cyclops: The red dot like those seen on most of Robin’s Birdarang became his eye. A Day in the Limelight: After his creation, he is given a more prominent role in “Jinxed”, “Little Buddies”, “Power Moves”, “Brian”, “Justice League Top Talent Idol Star”, “The Academy”, “Costume Contest”, and “The Overbite”.

characters.name: Beat Box
characters.description: Animate Inanimate Object: A living boombox. A Day in the Limelight: After his creation, he is given a more prominent role in “Little Buddies”, “Brian”, and “Power Moves”. They Killed Kenny Again: He was crushed thrice, the first time by Pain Bot, the second time by Robin, and the third time by a teenage mutant ninja turtle.

characters.name: Dave
characters.description: Savage Wolves: He's a wolf who is very confrontational and aggressive.

characters.name: Demon
characters.description: Art Evolution: Starting with Season 4, the demon's design has become more detailed, gaining pink eyes, slit irises, a rounder head and purple outlines. Ascended Extra: He started off as a throwaway gag in "Driver's Ed" as a random demon that Raven was trying to banish before she got interrupted. After this episode it returns a few more times with Raven still trying to banish it. Eventually it becomes Raven's Little Buddy with her seemingly earning its allegiance. Chekhov's Gunman: He was accidentally released by Robin and roamed Jump City throughout his first appearance in "Driver's Ed".
