He comes back at the very end of the episode to take out Ed, the main antagonist of the episode. Heel–Face Turn: In his first few appearances Raven attempted to banish him. Eventually he becomes Raven's Little Buddy. Living Shadow: Is a monster that looks like a sentient shadow.

characters.name: Super Robin
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Went from an one-time gag in "Super Robin" of Robin swapping his DNA with that and a robin, to becoming aRunning Gagand Robin's Little Buddy. The Bus Came Back: After a long absence, Super Robin makes a cameo in Season 9 in the episode "Winged Warriors". Running Gag: He has a habit of stealing someone's food and then grappling away. Uncatty Resemblance: His eyes look like Robin's mask. Uplifted Animal: He became smarter than the average bird after Robin tried to merge with him in a failed attempt to get powers.

characters.name: Universe Staff
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: His return as one of Robin's Little Buddies is surprising given that Robin had thrown him out in favor of his regular staff. Catchphrase: "Staff Meeting!" that he adopted from Robin. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Disappears from the series after the Season 2 finale. Replacement Goldfish: Robin decides to use him as his new staff after the Universe Tree refuses to grant him a new one, and he proves himself to be quite handy. This doesn’t last however, as Robin's old staff had managed to be repaired, leaving Robin to abandon him, left to be used as a plunger by Beast Boy. World Tree: It’s former status as the Universe Tree. It was able to grant the wishes of whoever stood before it. It’s implied to still have this ability as a mere branch.

characters.name: Sticky Joe
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Starting off as a throwaway one-off character, Sticky Joe ended up as a recurring character and has even gone tostar in his own episodes. Bit Character: He'll pop up every now and then to shout his catchphrase, "Howdy!" He does get a few episodes to himself, however. Canon Foreigner: He was created specifically for the show and doesn't have a comic book or 2003 counterpart. Catchphrase: "Howdy!" A Day in the Limelight: He gets the spotlight in "A Sticky Situation", "A Stickier Situation" and "Stickiest Situation".

characters.name: Sticky Joan
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: Like her male counterpart, she doesn’t exist in the original comics or cartoon. Catchphrase: "Howdy!", just like her husband. Eyes Always Shut: Just like her male counterpart, as she's hardly ever seen with them open. Happily Married: To Sticky Joe as of "Stickiest Situation". Look-Alike Lovers: Sticky Joe and Sticky Joan look nearly identical to one another.

characters.name: Albert "Berto" Jelenic
characters.description: Ambiguously Brown: Berto talks with a Mexican accent and has a Spanish sounding name, and might even have some Spanish heritage, he's a Caucasian male, who lives in the wannabe-Mexican community of San Pedro, LA and fully embraces the culture there. Author Avatar: He is a self-insert of Albert Jelenic, the father of the creator of the series,Michael Jelenic. Jewish Father: A mild variant of this. He complains that he wishes his son, would get a real job like being a longshoreman.noteIn real life, however, this is far from the case, as Albert is 100% supportive and very proud of his son being a cartoonist and absolutely sees it as a real job. Hence, why he even guest voices himself in the first place. Killed Off for Real: Following the unfortunate death of Albert Jelenic in 2019, the character he voiced was quietly but respectfullywritten off the show,even if they never explicitly mentioned him dying, with his final appearance in the show beingdedicated to him. Only Known by Their Nickname: Although his real name is Albert Jelenic and it's obvious this is true in both real-life and the series, the Titans still always call him "Berto".

characters.name: Dummy Robin
characters.description: Ambiguously Sentient Object: Robin was initially shown to control it like a typical ventriloquist dummy. However, in some still-frames during its time with the Justice League, it's shown to move completely on its own. This seemed to have been reversed in its next appearance. Sixth Ranger: Becomes the newest member of the Justice League after becoming the winner of the Justice League's Next Top Talent Idol Star. Ventriloquism: Itisa ventriloquist dummy of Robin after all. What Happened to the Mouse?: Dummy Robin doesn’t return alongside the Justice League in any futureJustice League's Next Top Talent Idol Starinstallments after the "Second Greatest Team Edition".

characters.name: Zippy's Pizza Delivery Guy
characters.description: Badass Normal: In spite of just being an ordinary pizza delivery guy, he manages to outwit two Titans who with the entire Titan Tower's advanced tech at their disposal. Despite Beast Boy and Cyborg's efforts, he manages to evade every obstacle they put in his way and always arrive on time to deliver his pizza. Catchphrase: "Hey Pizza!" Determinator: Beast Boy and Cyborg throw everything at them and he still manages to make it to the door. Unknown Rival: He seems completely unaware that Cyborg and Beast Boy are trying everything they can to get a free pizza by delaying his deliveries. Unstoppable Mailman: The episode never shows exactly how he gets to the Tower, under increasingly impossible odds, for each delivery.Subverted at the end when he fails to deliver an old man's pizza within 30 minutes. This causes Cyborg and Beast Boy toFreak Out.

characters.name: Raven's Emoticlones
characters.description: Adaptational Heroism: Marginally. Red Raven in the original series was a straight out antagonist that had to be defeated. This version while still very violent and aggressive, is for the most treated like a difficult ally that the Titans are willing to put up with. By the time of "Some of Their Parts", Robin has managed to gain enough control over Red Raven and placed her on his improved Titans team. Adapted Out: Raven has been limited to having only five different personalities, so there's no signs of Yellow (Smart) Raven, Green (Brave) Raven, or Brown Raven in this show. Big Eater: Orange Raven, she ate everything in the Titans' refrigerator. The clasp on her cloak is even acheeseburger. Composite Character: Orange Raven appears to take aspects from both her original series counterpart for representing Raven’s rudeness and Brown Raven representing her slothness. Decomposite Character: In the original show they were part of Raven's inner-psyche. While in the show they all become separate individuals as Raven'sLiteral Split Personality.

characters.name: Other Titan Emoticlones
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: The Yellow Beast Boy's specialty is being a human shield for the Titans. Lazy Bum: All 5 of them are lazy, especially the Purple Beast Boy who represents relaxation. Lazy Bum: The Orange Cyborg is a lethargic slob. Perpetual Frowner: Green Cyborg doesn't smile, which is justified since it represents his soldier side. Plucky Comic Relief: The Purple Cyborg represents his jokes side.

characters.name: Second Santa
characters.description: Accidental Truth: After we're initially given the impression that the other Titans made him up to mess with Starfire, it turns out that hedoesexist. Jetpack: What he travels with instead of a sleigh pulled by eight tiny reindeer. One-Shot Character: "Second Christmas" is his only appearance in the show. Polar Opposite Twins: He's skinny, clean shaven, wears a green tracksuit and travels by jetpack compared to First Santa, who is overweight, bearded, wears a red suit, and flies a sleigh pulled by eight tiny reindeer. Wish Fulfillment/Be Careful What You Wish For: He grants the Titans their wish of not having to wait a year for Christmas by causing an explosion in Titans Tower that puts them in a coma that they come out of on Christmas Eve.

characters.name: Sonia Conchita Hernández
characters.description: Cloudcuckoolander: How else are we supposed to explain why she falls in love with Silkie?noteAside fromRule of Funnythat is. Impossible Hourglass Figure: Her hips and bust are wider/larger than the majority of the other characters in the series, making her stand out even more. Interspecies Romance: Falls in love withSilkie. Latin Lover: A parody of theSoap Operaversion. Little Black Dress: In the second half of the episode.

characters.name: George Washington
characters.description: Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: Can summon the Statue of Liberty as an attack robot. False Teeth Tomfoolery: He's subjected to some gags about the misconception that he had wooden dentures. Flight: By having a bald eagle grab his back. Luckily, My Shield Will Protect Me: Can conjure a shield reminiscent ofCaptain America's first shield to deflect attacks. Politicians Kiss Babies: When competing with Robin in which of them should be the Teen Titans' leader, he at one point tries to kiss a baby, but Robin ruins it by bumping into Washington and making him accidentally hurt the infant with his wooden dentures.

characters.name: Little Girl
characters.description: Running Gag: Her running away via either screaming or crying, usually due to the Titans or villains shenanigans.

characters.name: Sea Creatures
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: The octopus. He is killed in his first appearance, and injured in his second. They Killed Kenny Again: Aqualad murdered them by making some sharks eat them in “Pirates”.

characters.name: Cool Turtle Dudes
characters.description: Lawyer-Friendly Cameo: They're basically theTeenage Mutant Ninja Turtlesin everything but name, beingSurfer Dude-accented terrapin ninja who love pizza. Trademark Favorite Food: Being pastiches of the Ninja Turtles, they of course like pizza. Uncertain Doom: After the Titans have beat them up, the Titans are last seen wearing their shells. Since the Turtles aren't seen again at this point, it's unclear whether the removal of their shells killed them like it would real-life turtles or if they're just unconscious andnaked.

characters.name: Polly Ethylene and Tara Phthalate
characters.description: A pair of “miracle molecules” with the ability to recycle into almost anything. Green Aesop: Appear in their titular episode in order to deliver one about recycling. Hair Substitute Feature: They both have, um, “molecular structure” as hair. Objectshifting: They can transfor- erm, “recycle” into anything that can be made of plastic, from water bottles to playground equipment to synthetic-fabric sweaters. Punny Name: They both have the first part of their chemical name be replaced by a similar-sounding girls’ name.

characters.name: Seagull
characters.description: Art Shift: In "Jinxed", the seagull's appearance was completely revamped, so it could resemble the seagull fromThe Little Mermaid. In "BBRAE", he was revamped to look like a girl. The Bus Came Back: The seagull has made dozens of return appearances, following his initial season, such as a cameo alongside the Crab in "Head Fruit" and being part of a mutation with the other rock animals in "Communicate Openly".The seagull was also perched outside of the Titans Tower in Teen Titans Go! to the Movies, despite the Sea Snail being the established rock animal at the time of it's airing. The seagull was also perched outside of the Titans Tower in Teen Titans Go! to the Movies, despite the Sea Snail being the established rock animal at the time of it's airing. Butt-Monkey: The seagull has been the victim of a lot of violence, such as getting eaten by a demon in "Driver's Ed", getting blasted by the Titan Robot against thescreenin "The Left Leg", getting knocked out of orbit and landing on the ground in "Garage Sale", getting eaten by the octopus in "Master Detective" and getting blown up in a nuclear explosion and later mutated in "Communicate Openly". The Cameo: In "Teen Titans Go! to the Movies". He and the other rock animals appeared behind the scenes on the set of Robin's movie.

characters.name: Crab
characters.description: Ambiguously Gay: In "How 'Bout Some Effort", the Crab and the Pelican were in love with each other. Both of the animals lack thetertiary sexual characteristicsto be female, so it's easy to assume that they're both two dudes in love. Art Shift: In "Jinxed" his design was completely revamped, so he could better resemble Sebastian fromThe Little Mermaid. The Cameo: In "Teen Titans Go! to the Movies". He and the other rock animals appeared behind the scenes on the set of Robin's movie. Convenient Replacement Character: To the Seagull. A Day in the Limelight: Plays a major role in “Master Detective” after earlier appearances had him do little besides reside on the rock outside Titans Tower.

characters.name: Pelican
characters.description: Ambiguously Gay: In "How 'Bout Some Effort", the Pelican and the Crab were in love with each other. Both of the animals lack thetertiary sexual characteristicsto be female, so it's easy to assume that they're both two dudes in love. Art Shift: The pelican looked significantly different in the theme song for the Island Adventure episodes. The Cameo: In "Teen Titans Go! to the Movies". He and the other rock animals appeared behind the scenes on the set of Robin's movie. Convenient Replacement Character: To the Crab. A Day in the Limelight: Was originally just an animal shown residing on the rock outside Titans Tower, but has a more important role in “Master Detective”.

characters.name: Octopus
characters.description: The Cameo: In "Teen Titans Go! to the Movies". He and the other rock animals appeared behind the scenes on the set of Robin's movie. Convenient Replacement Character: To the Pelican. A Day in the Limelight: Has a more important role in “Master Detective” after initially just being an animal appearing on the rock outside Titans Tower. Interspecies Romance: With the female seagull. Leprechaun: Dressed as one of these in "Beast Boy's St. Patrick's Day Luck and It's Bad", complete with the green hat, orange beard, and tap dancing shoes.

characters.name: Sea Snail
characters.description: Convenient Replacement Character: To the Octopus. Eldritch Abomination: In "Communicate Openly", he was mutated by a nuclear explosion, and he became genetically morphed together with all of the previous rock animals. High-Class Glass: Wore a top hat and a monocle in "What's Opera Titans?" One-Gender Race: As a snail, the Sea Snail would technically be considered a hermaphrodite. Outdated Outfit: In "Nostalgia is Not a Substitute for an Actual Story", the titans turned back time tothe 1980's, affecting the environment around them. This included the Snail, who ended up wearing shutter shades and spikes on it's shell.

characters.name: Sea Turtle
characters.description: All Animals Are Dogs: In "Witches Brew", the Sea Turtle howled like a wolf. Art Shift: In "The Viewers Decide", the Sea Turtle looked completely different, having a round head and larger more bulbous eyes with purple irises, similar to the eyes of the Snail. However, when it made its official debut in "Butt Atoms", it's appearance had significantly changed into the appearance he all know and love him for today. Convenient Replacement Character: To the Snail. Early-Bird Cameo: The Sea Turtle made an appearance in Season 5's "The Viewers Decide", where it was partially submerged in the water, slowly approaching the Sea Snail, signifying it's oncoming replacement in the soon-to-be next season. The Grinch: Is not a fan of the holidays. In "Beast Boy on a Shelf", the Sea Turtle was very grouchy about being decorated in Christmas lights, in "Witches Brew" he was scowling atop a pile of Halloween pumpkins, and in "Egg Hunt" he was being a real grump about having an Easter egg on his head.
